newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Wartime premier nominated for Bosnian government.
newsitem.headline: Wartime premier nominated for Bosnian government.

text.p: Bosnia's main Moslem party on Monday nominated wartime prime minister Haris Silajdzic to serve as co-chairman of the newly-formed central government, state television reported.
The move, which has to be formally approved by an inter-ethnic parliament, confirmed media speculation that Silajdzic would be chosen for the post.

Silajdzic resigned as premier after breaking with the nationalist Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) in 1995, and formed a rival party to back his own campaign for president in the country's first post-war elections this year.
Silajdzic lost to Alija Izetbegovic of the SDA, who now heads the three-man collective presidency.
According to the state television report, the executive board of the SDA named Silajdzic as its nominee for co-chairman in a weak central government known as the council of ministers.
Bosnia's Serb republic will name the other co-chair.
The co-chairs, one Serb and one Moslem, are supposed to function essentially as joint prime ministers.
The SDA also nominated Hasan Muratovic, who currently serves as prime minister, as minister of foreign trade.
Croat leaders are due to appoint the minister for foreign affairs and the Serbs will name a minister for civil affairs and communications.
After national elections, it took more than two months for Bosnia's factions to agree on the structure of the council of ministers.

Diplomats said the central government structure is supposed to ensure equal rights for Bosnia's three ethnic communities -- Moslem, Croat and Serb. Critics say the constitution contained in the peace treaty is a recipe for political gridlock.
